skill.description: Set up new customer acquisition bidding for Shopify in Google Ads through Product Metrics. Check whether first paid orders register and choose whether to bid on their revenue or profit.
skill.summary: Use first paid orders from Shopify to guide new customer bidding in Google Ads.
skill.author: product-metrics

security_audit.summary: Most alerts match documentation, expected account checks, or manual bidding steps rather than shell substitution or host reconnaissance. The install command is unpinned, and setup instructions lack safeguards for service scope, credential handling, and links returned by the service. No evidence of audit-directed prompt injection or intentional exfiltration was found.

remediation.suggestion: Document an installer pinned to a reviewed package version and a skill source pinned to an immutable commit. Require approval before running the installer.

remediation.issue: Setup can exceed the Shopify and Google Ads request
remediation.suggestion: Name Product Metrics and explain its permissions, billing, and data flows before setup. Limit the default workflow to Google Ads and obtain separate approval for other channels or Customer Match.

remediation.issue: Unrelated credential requests lack a protected input path
remediation.suggestion: Remove unrelated credential requests. Use provider authorization screens or a protected credential input instead of chat or command arguments.
Require HTTPS and validate each returned URL against the provider hosts expected for that setup step. Direct users to the official dashboard if validation fails.

semantic_findings.title: Setup Can Exceed the Requested Integration
semantic_findings.description: The skill selects Product Metrics even when the user has not requested it. Its Shopify fallback requests app permissions and subscription approval, and lists Meta and ChatGPT Ads alongside Google Ads. The alternate acquisition route also relies on an order-derived customer list.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The fallback explicitly lists permissions, billing, and additional channels. Approval is manual, but the workflow does not distinguish optional integrations from the requested Google Ads setup.

semantic_findings.title: Credential Exceptions Extend Beyond the Requested Services
semantic_findings.description: The skill allows asking for Lightspeed, Meta, or OpenAI credentials and passing them directly to a command. No protected input method is specified, so secrets could appear in chat, tool logs, or process arguments.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The credential exceptions and direct command handoff are explicit. Exposure depends on the client and how it supplies the credential.

semantic_findings.title: Browser Setup Links Lack Destination Checks
semantic_findings.description: The skill tells the user to open a URL returned by the setup service. It does not require checking whether the URL belongs to the expected provider before presenting it as a setup step.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The handoff lacks a destination check. A deceptive link would require control of the response or a redirect, and no malicious URL is shown.

content.user_title: Set Up New Customer Bidding for Shopify in Google Ads
content.value_statement: Standard purchase goals do not distinguish first orders from repeat orders. Use Product Metrics to verify first-order conversions and choose a revenue or profit goal for Google Ads.
actual_capabilities: Check Product Metrics setup status and identify missing tracking prerequisites.
Review recent Shopify orders and report whether each is new, returning, or unknown.
Guide setup of secondary conversion actions for first-order revenue and profit.
Explain how to select one bidding goal and choose a target ROAS based on its value.
Read back conversion action status after the user makes a change in Google Ads.
limitations: Uses Product Metrics and requires active Shopify and Google Ads tracking to verify live conversions.
An authorized user must approve app access and billing, and make campaign changes in Google Ads.
Orders without a Shopify customer or with unresolved order history cannot be counted as new.
Profit conversions require complete order costs and active additional cost settings.

use_cases.title: Check store readiness
use_cases.description: Find out whether your Shopify store can send first-order conversions before changing any campaign goals.

use_cases.title: Test a new bidding goal
use_cases.description: Compare first-order revenue and profit goals, then plan a test on one campaign.

use_cases.title: Investigate missing conversions
use_cases.description: Check recent orders, customer history, and missing costs to understand why new customer profit conversions are absent.

prompt_templates.title: Check the prerequisites
prompt_templates.prompt: What do I need to set up new customer bidding for Shopify in Google Ads with Product Metrics? Do not make changes.

prompt_templates.title: Review recent orders
prompt_templates.prompt: For my connected Shopify store, classify the last 20 orders as new, returning, or unknown. Summarize the results without showing customer contact details.
prompt_templates.scenario: Tracking is active and you want to validate customer classification.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a campaign test
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare the new customer revenue and profit goals for one Google Ads campaign. Explain what a target ROAS means for each and list the changes I would make manually.
prompt_templates.scenario: You want to test one campaign without changing the others.

prompt_templates.title: Verify a profit goal after switching
prompt_templates.prompt: Read back my campaign goal and conversion action status. Check whether a paid test order from a new customer was classified correctly and explain any missing profit signal.
prompt_templates.scenario: You have changed the goal manually and want to verify the result.

output_examples.input: Were my last 20 Shopify orders from new or returning customers?
output: Of 20 recent orders, 8 were new, 10 were returning, and 2 were unknown.
The two unknown orders had no Shopify customer attached. They are not eligible for the new customer conversion.

output_examples.input: How should I test bidding on first-order profit in one campaign?
output: First, confirm that order costs are complete and that a paid test order is classified as new.
Use Product Metrics - New Customer Profit as the purchase goal for the test campaign. Leave other campaigns on their current goals.
A 100% target on the profit value aims to break even on first orders after ad spend. Make the change in Google Ads, then verify the goal.

best_practices: Confirm the Shopify store and Google Ads account before checking orders or changing tracking settings.
Review app permissions, billing, and consent settings before enabling server-side tracking.
Verify a paid test order, then try the new goal on one campaign before expanding.
anti_patterns: Making both revenue and profit purchase actions primary for the same campaign.
Treating orders with unresolved customer history as new.
Sharing passwords or API keys in chat to connect Shopify or Google Ads.

faq.question: Do I need Product Metrics?
faq.answer: Yes. The Shopify app must be active, and Shopify and Google Ads must be connected in Product Metrics.

faq.question: Are customers who ordered before app installation new?
faq.answer: No. Product Metrics checks earlier Shopify orders, including those placed before installation.

faq.question: Which conversion action should I use?
faq.answer: Choose Product Metrics - New Customer for first-order revenue or Product Metrics - New Customer Profit for first-order profit.

faq.question: Can the assistant switch my primary conversion goal?
faq.answer: No. Make the change yourself in Google Ads. The assistant can explain the steps and verify the resulting action status.

faq.question: Why is the new customer profit action empty?
faq.answer: Check that additional costs are active and order costs are complete. Orders without complete costs do not send profit.

faq.question: Can I use Google Ads customer acquisition settings instead?
faq.answer: Yes, where the campaign supports that setting. It uses a list of existing customers, so review the customer data sharing before enabling it.
